run.rulesInOwnWords: 1) Six tanks in series; 1 = inlet, 6 = outfall. Each cycle runs 5 steps in order, and each step finishes for all six tanks before the next step starts. 2) Step 1 Inflow: add that cycle's scheduled inflow to each tank. Volume is not checked here. 3) Step 2 Weir overflow: go through the tanks in order 1 to 6. If a tank holds more than its volume, the excess moves to the next tank (from tank 6 it goes to outfall) and the tank is set to its volume. Because the order is sequential, overflow can cascade down the train in the same step. This is the only step that enforces volume. 4) Step 3 State check, using contents after Step 2: a STEADY tank at or above its upper mark becomes OVERLOADED. An OVERLOADED tank at or below its lower mark becomes STEADY. Every other tank keeps its state (hysteresis). Log each change. 5) Step 4 Discharge/return: work out every amount first from the Step 4 starting contents. STEADY gives floor(contents/4) and OVERLOADED gives floor(contents/2). Then apply all six at once. Each tank loses its amount. A STEADY amount goes to outfall. An OVERLOADED amount goes back to the previous tank (n-1), except tank 1, whose amount goes to outfall. Volume is not enforced, so any excess waits for the next cycle's Step 2 (or stays after cycle 5). 6) Step 5 Storm bypass: if the combined contents are strictly more than 38, every tank is halved (floor) and everything removed goes to outfall; log the cycle. A total of 38 or less does nothing. 7) The outfall total only grows. Balance: starting contents + all inflows = end contents + outfall.
run.balanceCheck: Left: starting contents 3+6+6+2+2+1 = 20, plus inflows 20+15+17+24+18 = 94, gives 114. Right: end contents 6+10+9+7+4+2 = 38, plus outfall total 76, gives 114. The two sides match.
run.notes: I used a short Python script for the arithmetic and checked cycle 1 by hand. Some results sit exactly on a rule threshold. In cycle 5 the Step 5 total is exactly 38, so the bypass did not fire. In cycle 2, T3 (4) and T5 (3) each sat exactly on their lower marks, and T1 (7) sat exactly on its upper mark. After cycle 5, T2 (10 vs 8) and T4 (7 vs 6) are left above their volumes from returned liquor, as the document specifies.
